title: Bidirectional Code Reuse in Software Redesign: An Action Research Study of Static Analyzers
abstract: arXiv:2604.07919v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Software redesign preserves functionality while improving quality attributes, but manual reuse of code and tests is costly and error-prone, especially in cross-repository redesigns. Focusing on static analyzers where cross-repository redesign needs often arise, we conduct a bidirectional study of the ongoing Soot/SootUp redesign using an action research methodology that combines empirical investigation with validated open-source contributions. Our study reveals: (1) non-linear migration that necessitates bidirectional reuse, (2) deferred reuse via TODOs, (3) neglected test porting, and (4) residual bug propagation during migrations. translated_title: 软件重设计中的双向代码复用：一项针对静态分析工具的行动研究
translated_abstract: 软件重设计在保留功能的同时改进质量属性，但手动复用代码和测试成本高昂且容易出错，尤其是在跨仓库重设计的场景下。我们聚焦于经常产生跨仓库重设计需求的静态分析工具领域，采用结合实证调查与经过验证的开源贡献的行动研究方法，对正在进行的 Soot/SootUp 重设计开展了双向研究。我们的研究揭示了以下现象：(1) 需要双向复用的非线性迁移，(2) 通过 TODO 延迟执行的复用，(3) 被忽视的测试移植，(4) 迁移过程中残留缺陷的传播。我们识别出追踪对应的代码和测试是核心挑战，并通过改造克隆检测技术来推导原始项目与重设计项目之间的代码映射以应对这一挑战。在研究中归纳出的语义复用模式指导下，我们提出了语义对齐分数（SAS），它结合了……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文以行动研究方法剖析 Soot/SootUp 跨仓库重设计中的双向代码复用问题，揭示了非线性迁移、测试移植被忽视与残留缺陷传播等关键现象，并提出基于克隆检测的代码映射方法与语义对齐分数（SAS）来追踪原始代码与重设计代码及测试的对应关系。
en_tdlr: Through an action research study of the Soot/SootUp cross-repository redesign, this paper reveals bidirectional code reuse challenges (non-linear migration, neglected test porting, and bug propagation) and proposes clone-detection-based code mapping along with a Semantic Alignment Score (SAS) to track corresponding code and tests between original and redesigned projects.
